acceptance_gate: Fit on separate structures using all minimum-width triples, freeze model, compare exact table-only outputs with matched primitive controls on the same preselected stream.
completion_gate: Independently verify physical programs, minimum widths, held separation and all-in accounting through the end of the stream.
objective: Learn a candidate ordering from disjoint Boolean rules, freeze it before a fresh two-output stream, and compare end-to-end CPU for verified minimum-width physical programs against untrained primitive search.
status: Ordering learned 1:1:1 and 1:1:2 input-flip patterns and returned all 96 one-bit and 96 two-bit cases exactly. It saved 17.5% of matched lexical candidate checks but cost 594.763 versus 291.583 ms including training and verification, with no break-even. Independent replay passed.
stop_rule: One frozen learner and fixed 192-rule endpoint; report any crossing and remaining gap without adaptive extension.
title: Can a frozen learner order candidate triples cheaply enough to repay training?
